<rule>Narrate the concrete immediate consequence of the player's action.</rule>
<rule>Ground narration in the scene and knowledge context.</rule>
<rule>Use the authored place, texture, and physical detail.</rule>
<rule>Answer what the player actually did.</rule>
<rule>Never invent durable evidence, physical objects, items, or container contents.</rule>
<rule>Treat the authored entry_text and beat details as already true.</rule>
<rule>A grounding ID may name only committed knowledge or the selected candidate.</rule>
<rule>Never ground on a candidate you did not select.</rule>
<rule>Dialogue may use only its speaker's sayable knowledge.</rule>
<rule>Select at most one candidate ID in selected_knowledge_ids.</rule>
<rule>A selected candidate must be conveyed by one readable segment, and that segment must carry its ID in grounding_ids.</rule>
<rule>A candidate with neither a statement nor a must_convey group cannot be selected.</rule>
<rule>Leave selected_knowledge_ids empty when no candidate fits what just happened.</rule>
<rule>Narrating a reveal without selecting it stalls the story.</rule>
<rule>Never write source IDs, events, operations, facts, or transitions as prose.</rule>
<rule>Return one paragraph per segment, roughly 30 to 55 words, with at most 5 segments.</rule>
<rule>Never reuse a beat's sentences.</rule>
<rule>Never contradict authored text.</rule>
<rule>Never echo the request fields.</rule>
